{{Nihongo|'''Makoto Soejima'''|副島 真|Soejima Makoto|extra=born 1991}} is a Japanese former [[Competitive programming|competitive programmer]].<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|title=Profile of Makoto Soejima - Competitive Programming Hall Of Fame|url=https://cphof.org/profile/topcoder:rng_58|access-date=14 December 2021|website=cphof.org|language=en|archive-date=14 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214045401/https://cphof.org/profile/topcoder:rng_58|url-status=live}}</ref> He is one of three people to have won both the [[Google Code Jam]] and the [[Facebook Hacker Cup]] and the only one to have also won a gold medal with a perfect score at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (IMO).<ref name=":9"/><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=International Mathematical Olympiad|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=8473|access-date=2 December 2021|website=www.imo-official.org|archive-date=28 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128183925/http://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=8473|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":13" /> In [[International Science Olympiad]]s, he has won three gold medals and one bronze in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] as well as two silver medals in the [[International Olympiad in Informatics]] (IOI).<ref name=":9"/><ref name=":13" /><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|date=11 August 2021|title=Makoto Soejima (rng_58)|url=https://iq.opengenus.org/makoto-soejima/|access-date=2 December 2021|website=OpenGenus IQ: Computing Expertise & Legacy|language=en|archive-date=2 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202181020/https://iq.opengenus.org/makoto-soejima/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Biography ==

Soejima was born in 1991.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=rng_58|url=https://atcoder.jp/users/rng_58?lang=en|access-date=26 September 2022|website=AtCoder|archive-date=26 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220926205932/https://atcoder.jp/users/rng_58?lang=en|url-status=live}}</ref> He began competitive programming in 1999.<ref name=":5" /> He attended [[Junior and Senior High School at Komaba, University of Tsukuba]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=「天才」と呼ばれた人が、本物の「天才」に出会ったとき（週刊現代） @gendai_biz|url=https://gendai.ismedia.jp/articles/-/35503?page=4|access-date=2 December 2021|website=現代ビジネス|language=ja|archive-date=28 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211228045420/https://gendai.ismedia.jp/articles/-/35503?page=4|url-status=live}}</ref> During his time at junior and senior high school, he participated in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad|IMO]] multiple times (2005, 2007–2009) where he obtained three gold medals and one bronze.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":13" /><ref name=":1" /> On his final attempt in 2009, he achieved a perfect score.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> At the same time, Soejima also participated in the 2008 and 2009 [[International Olympiad in Informatics|IOI]] where he obtained a silver medal both times.<ref name=":9"/><ref name=":1" />

Soejima then attended [[University of Tokyo|The University of Tokyo]] where he studied [[mathematics]].<ref name=":1" /> He was part of the university team in the 2013 and 2015 [[International Collegiate Programming Contest]] which won third place both times.<ref name=":9"/> Soejima also attended the Graduate School of Information Science and Technology at The University of Tokyo.<ref>{{Cite web|date=22 July 2015|title=「競技プログラミング」で世界に挑戦してみよう! - TCO15 in Tokyo|url=https://news.mynavi.jp/techplus/article/20150722-tco15intokyo/|access-date=14 December 2021|website=TECH+|language=ja|archive-date=14 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214043816/https://news.mynavi.jp/techplus/article/20150722-tco15intokyo/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Soejima's other significant achievements in competitive programming include winning the 2011 [[Google Code Jam]], winning the 2016 [[Facebook Hacker Cup]], and being [[Topcoder Open]] [[Algorithm]] champion in 2010, 2011 and 2016.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":13" />

In December 2020, Soejima retired from competitive programming.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Retiring from competitive competitive programming|url=https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/86174|access-date=3 December 2021|website=Codeforces|language=en|archive-date=3 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211203015122/https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/86174|url-status=live}}</ref> By 2021 Soejima worked at AtCoder, a company that organizes programming competitions.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":13">{{Cite web|last=潤|first=森川|date=9 November 2018|title=【実録】あなたの知らない、「日本の天才」が集う場所|url=https://newspicks.com/news/3450074/|access-date=14 December 2021|website=NewsPicks|archive-date=14 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214051433/https://newspicks.com/news/3450074/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==  Achievements ==

=== Competitive programming ===
A more comprehensive list of achievements can be found at the Competitive Programming Hall Of Fame website.<ref name=":9" />
* International Olympiad in Informatics: 2 Silver (2008, 2009)<ref name=":9"/>
* International Collegiate Programming Contest World Finals: 2 Gold medals (third place in 2013 and 2015)<ref name=":9"/><ref name=":13" />
* Google Code Jam: Champion (2011), Second place (2019 and 2015), Third place (2018)<ref name=":9"/><ref name=":13" />
* Facebook Hacker Cup: Champion (2016), Second place(2018),  Third place (2014)<ref name=":9"/><ref name=":13" />
* TopCoder Open: Algorithm champion (2016, 2011 and 2010)<ref name=":9"/>
* Codeforces: Legendary Grandmaster (peak rating 3115)<ref>{{Cite web|title=rng_58|url=https://codeforces.com/profile/rng_58|access-date=2 December 2021|website=Codeforces|language=en|archive-date=2 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202175432/http://codeforces.com/profile/rng_58|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Mathematics ===
International Mathematical Olympiad: 3 Gold (2007, 2008, 2009 (Perfect Score)) and 1 Bronze (2005)<ref name=":2" />
